The rule set of `app/globals.css` immediately before Phase 4 split it, frozen so the split can be checked as a move rather than believed as one.

The source is `app/globals.css` at commit 6bc7d42, the last commit that had one. Each row is `<enclosing at-rules> || <selector list> || <declarations>` with whitespace collapsed; `@media`, `@supports` and `@keyframes` blocks appear only as the at-rule context of the rules inside them, because a container declares nothing itself.

`scripts/style-invariants.test.mjs` rebuilds the same inventory from the stylesheets `app/styles/index.css` imports and compares the two as multisets, so a rule that was dropped, duplicated, or edited on its way out of the monolith fails the build with its own text. Order is deliberately not compared: the phase moved responsive rules to the file that owns their base rules, which reorders them on purpose. The order that decides a tie is checked separately, per repeated selector.

`excluded` names the stylesheets that were never part of the monolith and so cannot be compared against it. `substitutions` records the rules a phase did not move verbatim; each is matched by selector, so an unrecorded edit cannot hide behind them. An entry's `before` is one rule, or the list of rules a phase folded into one where two of them shared a selector under the same at-rules.

Phase 5 added 245 of them, against 4 from Phase 4, and that is the whole shape of what it did: it turned `npm run lint:css` into an error gate, and a rule that wrote a colour, a type size, a radius, a shadow or a stacking layer as a literal had to read the token instead. Each row names which of those it was. `rules` is untouched, which is the point -- the 1,869 rows still say what the monolith said, and the 245 edits are readable one at a time against them rather than reflowed into the baseline where nobody could see them.

This ledger is a provenance proof, not a standing budget, and the ratio above is how to tell when it has stopped being one. A phase that rewrites most of what it pins has nothing left to check against the frozen text, and should delete this file and the parity test with it rather than regenerate either to pass.

excluded.why: The token layer was already its own two files before Phase 4; none of its rules were ever in the monolith.

These five were `*.module.css` at Phase 3. Converting them renamed every class, so their rules are a rewrite rather than a move and there is no monolith text to compare them with. What holds them is the visual suite and `scripts/style-invariants.test.mjs`.
